title: 1968–69 National Hurling League
text:
{{Short description|38th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1968–69 National Hurling League |image = |dates =13 October 1968 – 18 May 1969 |teams = |team1 = Cork |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 7th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |two=Kildare |previous = [[1967–68 National Hurling League|1967–68]] |next = [[1969–70 National Hurling League|1969–70]] }} The '''1968–69 National Hurling League''' was the 38th season of the NHL, an annual [[hurling]] competition for the [[GAA county teams]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=5 August 2010|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}{{cite book |last= Smith|first=Raymond |date=1999 |title=Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games |location=Dublin, Ireland |page=208 |isbn=0950175870}} ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season | image=1968–69 National Hurling League Final programme.jpg | image_size = 250 |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1968-69 |winners=[[Cork GAA|Cork]]
7th National League title
Captain: [[Denis Murphy (Cork hurler)|Denis Murphy]] |relegated= |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer=[[File: Colours of Wexford.svg|border|20px]] [[Paul Lynch (hurler)|Paul Lynch]] (8-24) |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= 58 |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1967–68 National Hurling League|1967–68]] |nextseason=[[1969–70 National Hurling League|1969–70]] |updated=15 January 2017 }} [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1967-68 National Hurling League|1967-68 season]]. On 4 May 1969, [[Cork GAA|Cork]] won the title after a 3-12 to 1-14 win over [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the final. It was their 7th league title overall and their first since [[1952-53 National Hurling League|1952-53]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=5 August 2010|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} In spite of finishing at the bottom of their respective groups, neither [[Galway GAA|Galway]] of [[Laois GAA|Laois]] were relegated as there was no promotion-relegation this season.
